paul.name: Paul
paul.role: Writer in chains who asks Timothy to come soon
paul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
paul.importance: Paul writes in chains and tells Timothy not to be ashamed. He says his time of departure has come. He lists who left him and who stayed. He asks Timothy to come before winter. He asks for his cloak, the books, and Mark.
paul.connections: He calls Timothy his beloved child. He asks Timothy to bring Mark, a cloak, and the books.

timothy.name: Timothy
timothy.role: Paul’s beloved child, told to preach and endure
timothy.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
timothy.importance: Paul remembers Timothy’s tears and his family’s faith. He tells Timothy to guard sound teaching and to endure hardship. He tells him to preach the word and to correct others gently. Paul asks him to come soon.
timothy.connections: Paul calls him his beloved child. His grandmother Lois and mother Eunice had sincere faith.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: Lord who will judge, and who stood by Paul
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: Paul tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead. Paul says the Lord will judge the living and the dead. Paul says the Lord stood by him at his first defense. Paul expects the Lord to deliver him into his heavenly Kingdom.
jesus.connections: Paul calls him our Lord and Savior. Paul says he is risen and of David’s offspring.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Jesus.”

titus.name: Titus
titus.role: Worker who has gone to Dalmatia
titus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
titus.importance: Paul says Titus went to Dalmatia. The verse gives no reason and no task. It is one of three departures Paul lists as he asks Timothy to come.
titus.connections: Paul names him with Demas, who went to Thessalonica, and Crescens, who went to Galatia.

tychicus.name: Tychicus
tychicus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tychicus.importance: Paul says he sent Tychicus to Ephesus. The letter gives no reason. The note comes between the request to bring Mark and the request for the cloak.
tychicus.connections: Paul names him just after asking Timothy to bring Mark.
